haiku-low.q1: If row_count is 10,000 or fewer, the browser opens the small-export URL and the response is the CSV. Above that, a background job runs and emails a link. If row_count cannot be read, an error shows and no export starts.
haiku-low.q2: The click returns the existing queued or running export; no second job starts. That export may have different filters than the current URL. Recommendation: the page shows the returned export's filters.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The bucket's 7-day lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation. There is no cleanup job.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, retried after 60 and 300 seconds. After the third failure, the export is marked failed with an error, and an export_failed email is sent. The page shows Start again.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. Report rows are read only from it, never from the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: In the export record on the primary database. The page polls every 5 seconds while queued or running, and each page load fetches the latest record.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica, encodes them, and uploads 8 MB multipart parts. It never holds the whole report, only about 12 MB at most.
haiku-low.q8: Uploaded parts and the checkpoint (upload_id, part etags, last_row_id) are kept. The next attempt resumes from the last checkpoint, re-reading rows after last_row_id; unuploaded buffered rows are lost.
haiku-low.q9: Filters and columns are stored on the export record on the primary database. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job reads filters and columns from the record.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The second insert is rejected, and that request reads and returns the active record.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be completed at its key, and the record set to done, before the email. email_sent_at is written after a successful send. If rerun on done with no email_sent_at, the job only sends the email; if email_sent_at is set, it returns.
haiku-low.q12: The stream is aborted, so the browser reports a failed download, not a short file. Nothing is stored, and the page says Try again later.

sonnet.q1: By reports.row_count (unfiltered total, from the read replica): 10,000 or fewer = small path, the response to GET /api/reports/{id}/export.csv is the CSV streamed as an attachment download. Above 10,000 = POST creates an export record and background job; the user gets a 202 with export id/status, page shows status, and an emailed link valid 24 hours (plus Download button when done).
sonnet.q2: The insert is rejected by the partial unique index; the server reads and returns the existing active record (no second job starts). The user gets that existing export, which may have different filters than the current URL (open question 2: page should show the returned export's filters).
sonnet.q3: The emailed signed link works 24 hours. The file is deleted by the exports bucket's lifecycle rule 7 days after creation (no cleanup job). After 7 days the page shows "expired".
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts per job (waits 60s before attempt 2, 300s before attempt 3). Between attempts page shows "queued, retry N of 3". After the final failure: record set to failed with error text and completed_at, upload aborted if present, and an export_failed email sent; page shows failed with the error and a "Start again" button. (Exception: if the record is already done, it isn't marked failed.)
sonnet.q5: The read replica only; report rows are never read from the primary. (Export records live on the primary.)
sonnet.q6: In the export record (report_exports table) on the primary database. The page polls GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running, stopping at done/failed; on each page load it also fetches the latest record, so reopening later shows the current status (done with Download, failed, or expired after 7 days).
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads rows by keyset paging (5000 rows per read from replica, ~2-3 MB), encodes them into an 8 MB in-memory part buffer, uploads each full buffer as a multipart upload part (~115 parts), and never holds more than ~12 MB of report data. Object only appears on complete_multipart at the end. If an attempt has run over 20 minutes it checkpoints and continues in a new job.
sonnet.q8: Uploaded parts are kept (upload_id and checkpoint with parts list and last_row_id are saved on the record); nothing is visible at the object key until completion. Any unsaved in-memory buffer is lost. The next attempt resumes from the checkpoint: continues the same upload, starting after last_row_id, re-uploading the same part number if needed. (Lease: a different attempt can take over only if heartbeat is over 5 minutes old.)
sonnet.q9: They are sent in the JSON body of the POST (max 8 KB) and stored in the export record on the primary database. The job payload is only {export_id}; the job reads filters and columns from the record.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on report_exports (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running; the second insert is rejected and that request returns the existing active record.
sonnet.q11: The file must be finished: complete_multipart succeeded and the record is set to done (with completed_at and object key); the email is sent right after, then email_sent_at is written. On a rerun: if the record is done and email_sent_at is set, return without doing anything; if done with no email_sent_at, send only the email (no file rebuild); if failed, return.
sonnet.q12: The server aborts the connection mid-stream (does not end the response cleanly), so the browser reports a failed download rather than a short file. For stream over 50 seconds or more than 10,000 rows the page says "Try again later." If the replica errors before the first byte, it returns 503. Nothing is stored.
